sources.entry: Knowledge management is the collection of methods relating to creating, sharing, using and managing the knowledge and information.

summary.name: Knowledge management
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article describing knowledge management (KM), the organizational discipline of creating, sharing, using and managing knowledge and information.
use_cases: understanding how organizations capture and share knowledge
planning knowledge retention when employees leave
studying knowledge management theory for coursework
choosing KM strategies such as codification or personalisation
summary.what_it_does: The page is an encyclopedic overview of knowledge management. It covers the history of the field from the 1990s, the tacit versus explicit knowledge distinction, and Nonaka's SECI model. It also describes KM strategies such as codification and personalisation, a list of practices like communities of practice and after-action reviews, and categories of KM technology such as groupware, workflow, content management and enterprise portals. Additional sections cover knowledge retention, knowledge audits and knowledge protection methods.
notable: Covers SECI model of tacit and explicit knowledge conversion
Lists KM technology categories such as groupware, workflow, and enterprise portals
Includes sections on knowledge retention and knowledge audits
caveats: This is a concept article, not a software tool, so there is no product to download or use
Page text is partial and ends mid-section on knowledge protection
